artifacts.summary: Confirms the lean-lsp wrapper is an orphaned hand-edit (not a missing source-store provision), confirms the NixOS PATH export is not load-bearing today (elan is a NixOS system package reachable via /run/current-system/sw/bin alone), confirms both --lean-project-path and LEAN_PROJECT_PATH are genuinely supported by lean-lsp-mcp with CLI taking precedence, recommends retiring cslib's orphaned wrapper, and recommends recording a durable invariant that mcpServers command paths must never point inside a repo's disposable .claude/ deploy tree.

memory_candidates.content: On this NixOS machine, elan is installed as a system package: /run/current-system/sw/bin/lake and /run/current-system/sw/bin/lean are symlinks into the elan Nix store path. A bare `uvx <tool>` (or any subprocess) needs only /run/current-system/sw/bin on PATH to reach a working Lean toolchain -- user-level ~/.elan/bin PATH exports are redundant on this machine. Verified empirically with `env -i PATH=/run/current-system/sw/bin:/usr/bin:/bin ... lake env lean --version` succeeding against a real project.

lean-lsp-mcp's CLI accepts --lean-project-path AND reads LEAN_PROJECT_PATH from the environment; when --lean-project-path is passed, the source explicitly overwrites os.environ[LEAN_PROJECT_PATH] before the server reads it, so CLI takes precedence over env when both are present. Both conventions are individually valid against the real server interface -- a divergence between two call sites using different conventions is not by itself evidence one of them is wrong.

MCP registration durable invariant candidate: an mcpServers command path in ~/.claude.json or .mcp.json must never point inside a repository's own .claude/ deploy tree, because that tree is disposable and regenerated wholesale (rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). A command path violating this looks configured until the next regeneration or a fresh clone, then fails as a silent ENOENT -- exactly the failure mode observed with an orphaned lean-lsp-mcp-wrapper.sh hand-edit.
